name: Lemon and garlic chicken traybake
subtitle: With new potatoes and green beans
description: Everything roasts in one tin while you get on with something else.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Halve any large potatoes so they're all about the same size.
Cut the onion into wedges. Squash the garlic cloves with the flat of a knife but leave the skins on.
Put the potatoes, onion and garlic in a large roasting tin. Add the oil, oregano, a good pinch of salt and some pepper, and toss it all together.
Sit the chicken thighs on top, skin side up if they have skin. Season them. Halve the lemon and squeeze one half over everything, then tuck both halves into the tin.
Roast for 25 minutes.
Scatter the green beans around the chicken, give the potatoes a shake and roast for another 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes are golden.
Squeeze the soft roasted garlic out of its skins and stir it through the potatoes before serving.

name: Sticky soy salmon with greens
subtitle: And a pan of jasmine rice
description: A quick glaze of soy, honey and ginger. Ready in about 20 minutes.
steps: Rinse the rice, then cook it in a pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes. Drain and keep it covered.
Meanwhile, grate the ginger and garlic into a small bowl. Stir in the soy sauce and honey.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the salmon skin side down and cook for 4 minutes without moving it.
Turn the salmon over, pour in the soy mixture and let it bubble for 2 to 3 minutes, spooning the glaze over the fish until it's sticky.
Lift the salmon onto a plate. Halve the pak choi lengthways and cook it in the same pan for 2 minutes, turning it in what's left of the glaze.
Slice the spring onions. Serve the salmon on the rice with the pak choi, and scatter over the spring onions and sesame seeds.

name: Slow cooker beef and ale stew
subtitle: Put it on in the morning, eat it at teatime
description: Ten minutes of chopping, then the slow cooker does the rest. Good with mash or crusty bread.
steps: Toss the beef in the flour with a pinch of salt and some pepper.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and brown the beef in two batches, a couple of minutes per batch. Tip it into the slow cooker. This step is optional, but it gives a deeper flavour.
Chop the onion, carrots and celery. Halve the mushrooms. Add them all to the slow cooker.
Pour the ale into the hot frying pan and scrape up any bits stuck to the bottom. Stir in the stock, tomato puree and thyme, then pour it over the beef.
Add the bay leaf, put the lid on and cook on low for 8 hours, until the beef falls apart when you press it with a spoon.
Take out the bay leaf, taste and add more salt or pepper if it needs it.

name: Creamy mushroom and spinach pasta
subtitle: Midweek comfort in 20 minutes
description: Mushrooms fried until golden, a splash of cream and a handful of spinach.
steps: Cook the pasta in a large pan of salted boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes. Before you drain it, scoop out a mugful of the cooking water.
While the pasta cooks, slice the mushrooms. Heat the oil in a frying pan over a high heat and fry them for 5 to 6 minutes, until golden. Don't stir them too often.
Crush the garlic, add it to the mushrooms and cook for 1 minute.
Turn the heat down, pour in the cream and let it bubble for a minute.
Add the drained pasta and the spinach and stir until the spinach wilts. Loosen the sauce with a splash of the pasta water.
Grate in most of the parmesan, season with pepper and serve with the rest of the parmesan on top.

name: Chickpea and spinach curry
subtitle: With rice and a spoonful of yoghurt
description: A mild, store-cupboard curry. Add a chopped chilli if you like it hotter.
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Finely chop the onion. Heat the oil in a saucepan over a medium heat and soften the onion for 6 to 8 minutes.
Grate in the garlic and ginger, add the curry powder and stir for 1 minute until it smells toasty.
Drain the chickpeas and add them with the chopped tomatoes and coconut milk. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts. Taste and add salt.
Serve with the rice and a spoonful of yoghurt on top.

name: Ginger pork noodle stir-fry
subtitle: Faster than a takeaway
description: Pork mince, crunchy veg and soft noodles in a sweet and salty sauce.
steps: Cook the noodles according to the packet instructions, then drain and toss them in the sesame oil so they don't stick.
Slice the pepper and cut the carrot into thin matchsticks. Grate the ginger and garlic.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan over a high heat. Add the pork mince and fry for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until it's browned and a little crispy.
Add the ginger and garlic and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the pepper, carrot and sugar snaps and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the noodles, soy sauce and hoisin and toss everything together until hot.
Slice the spring onions and scatter them over to serve.

name: Halloumi and roasted veg couscous
subtitle: With a lemony yoghurt dressing
description: Roast the veg, fry the halloumi, and fork it all through fluffy couscous.
ingredients: a small handful of fresh mint
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan).

Chop the courgette, pepper and onion into bite-sized pieces. Toss them in a roasting tin with 1 tbsp of the oil, the cumin, salt and pepper. Roast for 20 to 25 minutes, until soft and charred at the edges.
About 10 minutes before the veg is ready, put the couscous in a bowl, pour over the hot stock, cover with a plate and leave for 5 minutes.
Mix the yoghurt with a squeeze of lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Slice the halloumi. Heat the rest of the oil in a frying pan and fry the slices for 1 to 2 minutes on each side, until golden.
Fluff up the couscous with a fork and stir in the roasted veg and most of the mint.
Top with the halloumi and the rest of the mint, and spoon over the yoghurt dressing.

name: Turkey tacos with quick tomato salsa
subtitle: Build-your-own at the table
description: Lean mince with smoky spices, a fresh salsa and soft tortillas.
ingredients: a small handful of fresh coriander
steps: For the salsa, finely chop the tomatoes, red onion and most of the coriander. Mix them with the juice of half the lime and a pinch of salt.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the turkey mince and fry for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.
Stir in the paprika, cumin and tomato puree with a splash of water. Cook for 2 minutes more and season with salt.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or in the microwave for 20 seconds.
Shred the lettuce and grate the cheese.
Put everything on the table and let everyone fill their own tacos. Cut the rest of the lime into wedges to squeeze over.

name: Sausage and bean one-pot
subtitle: A cosy weeknight bake
description: Sausages browned and simmered with beans and tomatoes. Serve with crusty bread.
ingredients: a small handful of fresh parsley
steps: Heat the oil in a deep frying pan or casserole and brown the sausages all over for about 5 minutes. Lift them out and cut each one into three.
Chop the onion and pepper and cook them in the same pan for 5 minutes until soft.
Crush in the garlic, add the paprika and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the tomatoes. Drain the beans and add them with the Worcestershire sauce and the sausages.
Simmer with the lid off for 15 minutes, until the sauce is thick and the sausages are cooked through.
Season, then scatter over chopped parsley to serve.

name: Thai green chicken curry
subtitle: With green beans and sticky rice
description: Shop-bought paste makes this a quick one. Use as much as you dare.
ingredients: a small handful of fresh basil
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Trim the green beans and cut them in half.
Heat the oil in a wok or saucepan over a medium heat. Fry the curry paste for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and stir to coat it in the paste. Cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk, bring it to a simmer and add the beans. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the fish sauce and the juice of half the lime. Taste and add more of either if it needs it.
Serve with the rice, the basil leaves on top and lime wedges on the side.

name: Cheese and leek frittata
subtitle: With a simple green salad
description: Eggs, soft leeks and cheddar, finished under the grill. Leftovers are good cold the next day.
steps: Slice the potatoes thinly and boil them for 6 minutes until just tender. Drain.
Meanwhile, slice the leek. Melt the butter in an ovenproof frying pan over a medium heat and cook the leek gently for 6 to 8 minutes until soft.
Heat the grill to high.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and some pepper. Grate in most of the cheese.
Add the potatoes to the leeks, pour in the eggs and cook over a low heat for 5 minutes, until the edges have set.
Scatter the rest of the cheese on top and put the pan under the grill for 3 to 4 minutes, until puffed and golden.
Whisk the olive oil with the mustard and a pinch of salt, toss the salad leaves in it and serve with wedges of frittata.

name: Lamb kofta flatbreads
subtitle: With garlicky yoghurt and a crunchy salad
description: Spiced lamb shaped into little sausages and grilled. Messy, in a good way.
ingredients: a small handful of fresh mint
steps: Heat the grill to high and line a baking tray with foil.
Mix the lamb with the cumin, coriander, a good pinch of salt and some pepper. Divide it into 6 and squeeze each piece into a short, fat sausage shape.
Put the koftas on the tray and grill for 8 to 10 minutes, turning halfway, until browned and cooked through.
Grate the garlic into the yoghurt, add a pinch of salt and stir.
Chop the cucumber and tomatoes, finely slice the onion and mix them with most of the mint.
Warm the flatbreads for a minute under the grill.
Spread the flatbreads with the garlic yoghurt, add the salad and the koftas, and scatter over the rest of the mint.
